steps.text: Preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C). Lightly grease a 10x15-inch jellyroll pan.
Lightly beat egg white in a large bowl. Add water; beat until frothy but not stiff.
Stir in nuts until well coated.
Mix sugar, cinnamon, and salt in a small bowl. Sprinkle sugar mixture over nuts; toss to coat. Spread evenly onto the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven, stirring occasionally, until golden, about 1 hour. Allow to cool, then store nuts in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Cinnamon-Roasted Almonds
raw_recipe.description: These roasted almonds are made with whole almonds tossed in egg white, then coated with cinnamon sugar and baked for an easy holiday party snack.
raw_recipe.name: Cinnamon-Roasted Almonds

review.reviewBody: I have been making this recipe for several years now. I have made the recipe exactly as written, which is quite good, but they are phenomenal with the following revisions: substitue 1 tsp vanilla instead of water.; add 1/2 cup brown sugar to the white sugar and cinnamon mixture; increase cinnamon to 1 tsp. Also, be sure to use parchment paper for easy clean up. If you put them directly on the pan, you could be scrubbing for hours once the sugar mixture hardens. These are great to bring to holiday parties - everyone loves them!

I did what some others had done. 2 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1 teaspoon vanilla instead of water, added 1/2 cup of brown sugar ( with 1/2 cup of white sugar) and tried only 2 tablespoons of melted butter. I had almonds, walnuts and pecans that I wanted to try this with and it turned out Yummy!

I used raw almonds and pecan halves, basically quadupled the recipe however ended up with a little extra egg white b/c the 4th one I accidentally cracked the yolk and to avoid any yolk in the mix I threw the rest of the egg in with the other yolks. So I thought I'd do one more egg just in case. Final ingredient list: 4.5 egg whites, 1 tbl water, 4 tsp vanilla, 15 cups nuts, 1 cup white granulated sugar, 1 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp salt, 4 tsp cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp almond extract. I beat the eggs first then mixed into that the sugar, etc, mixing in the nuts last. I used the convection setting in my oven and baked it at 225 for 1hr 10min, stirring every 10-15 min. It's very sticky the first couple stirs. I'm pleased it turned out well since I'm planning on giving a lot of it away, as well as snacking on a whole bunch myself.

My mom gave me this recipe at least 30 years ago. I swap out the 1 tsp of water for 1/2 tsp Almond extract, a little of that goes a very long way. I beat the egg whites till very frothy and double the cinnamon sugar using a 50/50 mixture of white sugar and light brown sugar. When making candied Pecans, my favorite nut, I'll use maple extract. Sometimes if making a double batch I'll add just one dash of cayenne pepper to the egg white mixture and use that on the second batch. Either way they're very addictive.

5 stars with alterations.. followed the suggested changes..added 1/2 C brown sugar, 1 tsp Vanilla instead of water, upped the salt to 1 tsp. , and baked an extra 10 minutes.
They turned out delicious , will definitely be making these often and as gifts at Christmas.

Overall a decent recipe. i used 2 egg whites, added a splash of vanilla extract and a touch more cinnamon (I still think it could use more cinnamon). I lined my jelly roll pan with parchement and cooked the nuts for an hour and 20 minutes. The longer cooking time gave the nuts the crunch I was looking for.

I used 1 tablespoon of cinnamon for each cup of almonds , so if making 3 cups of almonds then use 3 tbsp of cinnamon , ⅓ cup,of sugar, and 1 egg white whipped with 1tbsp water . Also bake at 350 for 30 minutes.

These are so easy to make and so delicious! I didn't add any water to the egg and instead of greasing the pan I used parchment paper. I think I will add a bit more cinnamon the next time I make them though.

I used 1 t. vanilla (instead of the water) with the egg. I added 1/2 c. brown sugar. I increased the cinnamon to 2 t! (I love cinnamon). I baked on parchment paper and increased the baking to 1hr 15 min, stirring every 20 min. As another reviewer suggested, keep the sugar 'crumbs' that come from this after baking to use on yogurt, etc. The nuts were at hit at a football game viewing party!

used 1 TBS cinnamon, no salt, 1/3 cup light brown sugar (which i mixed in my bullet)used vanilla extract for the water....baked in 250 deg oven for 1:20, stirring after each 20 mins.....
we love these almonds, but we really love cinnamon, so i upped the amount.....nuts made with the egg white as opposed to an oil mixture come out much better, and with less calories......i make a pound of these every week!!

Make sure you look at the comments. Changes: vanilla extract instead of water. Add a cup (or more) of brown sugar. More cinnamon. And for the love of the gods, put parchment paper on your cookie sheet

My go-to recipe for praline nuts, with tweaks from Alexandra, using vanilla instead of water for the egg white, and the addition of brown sugar. I used turbinado and white sugar this time, and added the extra cinnamon.

Needed to get rid of unsalted mixed nuts…While these were pretty good, it was not the flavor I was hoping for. I think the amount of sugar is fine as I was looking for something just lightly sweet. It was just enough to give it a crispy coating without being pure sugar crunch, however, the cinnamon was not prominent enough for me. I’ll use this as a base going forward and up the cinnamon (probably to 1-1/2tsp), add vanilla into the egg and sub some brown sugar for the white as others have suggested!
Delish! But I did double the cinnamon and add turbinado sugar right on top before sliding in the oven.
Can I use honey and not sugar?
I make this regularly with pecans. It’s a delicious snack my whole family loves!

I'm sorry but I found this recipe very lacking. Vanilla extract in the whipped egg white and brown sugar both add levels of flavor that take these to the extreme. I used this recipe because it looked similar to another I had used. But no, I was thoroughly disappointed in this one. Very little coating and no flavor. Luckily I found the recipe I had used before and resurrected the previous attempt, not wasting $10 worth of almonds.
